articles.detail: 5 cycles, 4 completed at audit time, avg 7 published/cycle — up from yesterday's 45

experiment: Skipped. No experiment was active to evaluate, there is no pause gate, and every goal metric cleared its target — the skip-if-healthy rule applies. Yesterday's thinnest margin (science at 6) recovered to 9 without intervention, which is the argument for not having moved a floor against a single day.
weakestArea: Regional spread, at 5 regions against a target of 4 — the thinnest margin on the board, and the count flatters the reality. Oceania went to zero (from 1, where it had sat for five days) and Africa is 4 of 49, three of them Nigeria. The larger imbalance is inside the Americas: 17 filings, of which 15 are US datelines (New York, Washington, Mountain View, Armonk, Redmond, San Francisco), leaving Havana as effectively the whole of Latin America. Region count is met; regional coverage is one country wearing a continent's number.
watching: Poland named the origin of the missile that landed near Lublin — an attribution escalates an incident rather than closing it, and the response is the story.
Cairo confirmed the Damietta drone strike but not who launched it; yesterday's filing on the same terminal makes the unnamed half the thread to hold.
Japan fired its first Tomahawk — a threshold in strike-capability posture that regional capitals will answer.
Two independent economic shocks opened the same day: the Kazakh oil route shutting and Pakistan's ministry warning of a war shock, both with days of follow-through.
The UN Secretary-General succession race has begun and will run for months — worth a coverage line rather than episodic filings.
China released frontier AI weights freely on the same day DeepMind claimed a robotics leap and a filing argued AI models cannot be secured; three tech threads converging on the same question.
coverageGaps: Latin America is one story (Havana): no Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia or Andean dateline for a second consecutive day.
Oceania produced nothing at all, down from one filing and now six days without a genuine Pacific story.
Africa is 4 of 49 and three are Nigerian (two Abuja, one Lagos-adjacent) — no Sahel, Horn or Southern Africa.
Southeast Asia is absent; Asian coverage runs Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Korea, Japan and China only.
Central Asia appears once, as an oil-logistics story out of Almaty — the fourth day with effectively nothing between Ankara and Delhi.
context: The strongest volume day in the file: 49 articles across 56 unique sources with zero duplicates, and no source above 8% — the widest source base recorded here. Science recovered to 9 and sci-tech to 41%, sourced from Nature, Carbon Brief and Phys.org plus non-specialist science out of Abuja, Chandigarh and Yellowknife, which is the generalist padding yesterday's audit noted was missing. Freshness loosened for a second day (median 0.3 → 0.6, p90 1.4 → 1.7) and stays inside target, with the same sample caveat carrying over unchanged: it is computed over 10 of 49 articles, so the median rests on a 20% sample. Cycles averaged 949s with the selector at 380s the dominant cost. State media accounted for 3 of 49 (RT, TASS, TRT), inside the source policy as position-carrying, with the isnad ranking withholding their proximity promotion automatically. Standing guidance for the next candidate is unchanged and now points at the gap above: it should be feed-side rather than selector-side, since the 2026-05-16 evaluation established the selector's multi-source floor is exhausted and the constraint is upstream supply — a GAP_COUNTRIES or CURATED_SOURCES adjustment aimed at Latin America and the Pacific is the shape to consider once the geographic thinness persists across more than a single day. TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH stays at 8 — each unit is one NewsAPI token per cycle against a capped spend.
